newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian sorghum market fairly stable - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australian sorghum market fairly stable - Grainco.

text.p: The southern Queensland sorghum market remained relatively stable last week, with some grower selling interest in July-August at levels around A$128-A$130 a tonne on farm, Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd said.
Consumer buying interest seems to be centred around the fourth quarter, with some October-December business traded late in the week into both the Brisbane and Downs markets, it said.

With growers on the central and southern Darling Downs likely to plant barley until at least the last week of July, the market still has a couple of weeks before winter crop planting are finalised, Grainco said in its weekly market report.
In central Queensland, prices continue to be influenced by the excellent progress of the U.S. corn crop.

With export values currently trading around A$110 a tonne delivered port, some central Queensland sorghum is making its way into the southern market. However, logistics will continue to restrict the tonnage moving south in the near term, it said.
Early barley harvest yields in Southern Europe are above expectation which has continued to bring current export prices under pressure.
Recent international feed barley price reports are equivalent to US$125 a tonne fob Australian port.

Australian December/January prices have remained relatively stable, given the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) latest Australian barley crop estimate of 4.15 million tonnes, down 37 percent on 1996/97 production of 6.63 million, mainly due to El Nino concerns.

Australian southern barley plantings are 80 percent complete. In Queensland, falls of 25-50 mm are urgently required across the southern and central Downs in the next two weeks to achieve early planting estimates of 150,000 hectares.
Old crop feed barley prices finished the week unchanged at A$175 a tonne delivered Brisbane for June/July, reflecting a premium over export prices.
New crop values finished the week at A$153 for the November-December and A$158 for strict October delivery.
New corp malting barley values remain supported in the international market and finished the week at A$183 delivered Brisbane port.
Subdued activity persists in the cottonseed market.
Ginning is approaching completion in many areas, with Downs gins finalising processing by late June.
Not a lot of seed remains to be sold by growers in New South Wales (NSW) or Queensland. As ginning draws to a close small parcels of seed are becoming available, but this is limited.
Grainco said it does not appear that there is a larger volume of seed to come on to the market in July as was expected in some quarters of the market.
Demand for seed has been seen from both domestic and export consumers. Drier conditions in Queensland and northern NSW has prompted interest in cottonseed for winter usage.
Export demand remains open for the October 1997 through March 19988 period, with good inquiry from Japan and Korea.

Recent bulk cottonseed export business had the effect of tightening the Australian supply and demand equation, thus bringing a sense of urgency to prospective exporters purchasing. Downs gins are trading at A$155 a tonne ex gin for ginning period delivery to domestic consumers.
Apart from ongoing old crop shipments against existing commitments, there has been a dearth of activity in pulses.
All old crop chickpea product has been committed to consumption in either the domestic or export markets, and there is little interest from the Sub-Continent for new crop, it said.
Price indications for the new crop improved to A$320 a tonne delivered port basis for Queensland chickpeas. Indicative prices for faba beans remains at A$240 to A$250 a tonne.
Prices moved lower with sunflowers finishing the week at A$322 a tonne delivered Newcastle abd Brisbane for July/August.

Central Queensland sunflower prices were down to A$277 to A$282 a tonne delivered central Queensland (depending on location) for the July/August delivery period. New crop soybean prices moved lower at A$390 delivered Brisbane for July.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9372-1800
